html:
SMTO-LLM-0037 — An older retry attempt ran out of time

GUID: b9fb4e40-8d85-43d9-a32c-e9016f1ddfec
Slug: llm-constrained-recovery-timeout
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • This message comes from an older SMTO version that gave the model's retry a fixed time limit. Current SMTO keeps waiting as long as the model is making progress.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and open Limits and recovery. That is where the retry waiting time (Recovery timeout) and the optional total limit (Recovery deadline) are set.
  2. Leave Recovery deadline at 0 unless you want a firm cap. Raise Recovery timeout only if your model often pauses for a long time, then select Save Main. Recovery timeout only counts time with no progress, so a model that is still working isn't cut off.
  3. Start a new task to use these values. A resumed task keeps the time limits it started with.

What success looks like

  • Retries keep going while the model makes progress, and the task finishes or shows a newer, more specific message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change unrelated time limits or budgets to clear this old message; they control different things.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model request timed out while a legacy constrained-recovery profile was active, so the record maps to the historical llm_constrained_recovery_timeout identity; current recovery uses a progress-reset inactivity allowance and an optional total deadline instead.

What this means

  • An older runtime stopped recovery at its constrained-generation deadline. Current recovery instead uses a progress-reset inactivity allowance, defaulting to 300 seconds. A separate total recovery deadline is optional and disabled by default. Earlier completed operations retain their receipts.

Why this can happen

  • A historical constrained-recovery deadline elapsed before a usable decision arrived.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the retained recovery profile and effective request, no-action and generation limits; the earliest applicable limit controls this attempt.

How to fix it

  • This identity is assigned only when an llm_request_timeout carries a recovery_profile starting with constrained_, which current code no longer produces (current profiles are recovery_<mode> and brain_freeze_disabled). Current recovery uses Recovery timeout (inactivity, default 300 s, 30–1800, reset by progress) and an optional Recovery deadline (0 uses the task deadline). Review both under Limits and recovery for the role in Settings › Setup › Model routing; changes apply to new tasks, and Resume keeps the task's captured timing values.
  • Inspect Recovery inactivity timeout and Total recovery deadline in Model Configuration. Saved inactivity values stay unchanged; a total deadline of 0 is Off. Changed limits apply to new tasks; Resume keeps saved timing values.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Constrained-recovery Timeout: model-configuration / llm_constrained_recovery_timeout_seconds. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Recovery continues while meaningful progress arrives, subject to any explicit total deadline and resource limits.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-LLM-0001 — Model request timed out
  • SMTO-EXE-0005 — A command ran too long and SMTO stopped it
  • SMTO-CTX-0001 — The AI model said your request was too long for it
  • SMTO-LLM-0015 — The model ran out of room before finishing its reply
